behaviour: Written on every update (FP5L.js line 118); persists across flights.
Adds each per-update drop in the sim's total fuel of more than 0 and less than 2 L (line 107).
Resets to 0 when the total rises by more than 0.5 L in one update, i.e. at the refuel (line 108).

Not in this file, not in KIT1. The strip's own reading of L:NK_ST_FP5L_USED (below) is a separate, direct LocalVar read — it does not go through nk_telemetry.py at all.

price.note: The Ramp tab's live default (fields.LPCS.fuel_per_litre), fixed at build time — the strip has no per-field pricing because the wear model has no concept of which aerodrome you're at ('No NK_ variable exists: Aerodrome fees, landings by field'). A price change means a new build and a sim restart, same as every other strip price.

strip_accumulation_rule.accumulation: On every CONFIRMED read (see reload_safety below), in this exact order: (1) compute delta = current L:NK_ST_FP5L_USED − L:NK_LG_FUEL_BASELINE_L; (2) if delta > 0, add delta to L:NK_LG_FUEL_L_TOTAL — if delta <= 0, add nothing (a drop means FP5L.js reset the counter at a refuel, and must never post a negative cost); (3) THEN, regardless of the sign of delta, set L:NK_LG_FUEL_BASELINE_L = current L:NK_ST_FP5L_USED. Step 3 is mandatory even when step 2 added nothing: if the baseline were left at its pre-refuel value, the next read's delta would be computed against a stale, too-high baseline and would go negative too, silently swallowing every litre burned after the refuel. Baseline tracks 'last confirmed reading', full stop — it is not conditioned on whether that reading contributed litres.

persisted_state.L:NK_LG_FUEL_L_TOTAL: Running total litres accumulated this way. Persisted. Multiplied by strip_accumulation_rule.price.eur_per_litre at display time to fold into the strip's running euro total — litres are stored, not euros, so a future price rebuild does not require re-deriving historical litres from an old blended euro figure.
persisted_state.L:NK_LG_FUEL_BASELINE_L: The L:NK_ST_FP5L_USED value as of the last CONFIRMED read, updated every confirmed read per step 3 above regardless of delta sign. Advances in lockstep with L:NK_LG_BASELINE_MXLOG / L:NK_LG_BASELINE_TACH in STRIP_SPEC.md — never updated independently of the main cursor, and never skipped just because a given read didn't add litres.

strip_accumulation_rule.reload_safety: Gated by the same (NK_ST_MX_LOG, NK_ST_TACH) cursor as every other posting. On a reload/crash read (posting_cursor.rule_reload_or_crash), do not update L:NK_LG_FUEL_BASELINE_L and do not touch L:NK_LG_FUEL_L_TOTAL — exactly as no other posting happens on a reload. This is why the baseline is a separate persisted variable rather than re-reading FP5L_USED cold each time: it lets a reload leave the fuel accumulator exactly where it was, the same guarantee the maintenance/hours cursor already gives.
strip_accumulation_rule.laptop_book_unaffected: The laptop ledger keeps billing fuel exactly as in read_rule/fallback above — per-field priced, from the same FP5L_USED-before-uplift reading where available. This rule only concerns the strip's own separate running total.

rule_scaled_continuous.billing_normalisation: To price a service/repair, divide the OBSERVED condition loss by the R that was in force when it happened, so a part serviced after 6 minutes of sim time at x1000 is billed as 6 minutes' worth of REAL wear, not 6 minutes × 1000.

rule_scaled_by_r_only.billing_normalisation: Same principle: divide observed loss by R before pricing.

rule_starter_capped.spec_ref: SPEC §2.2 ('the rate factor is capped at 100')
rule_starter_capped.billing_normalisation: Divide by min(R, 100), not R — the wear model treats x100 and x1000 identically for the starter, so the same starter cost applies at either setting.

rule_never_scaled.note: No adjustment needed at any Wear rate setting; scheduled checks and hourly reserves already price off real elapsed hours.

rule_r_zero.rule: No loss accrues at all. Bill nothing for wear at this setting. Never divide by 0 — R=0 short-circuits before any normalisation formula runs.

rule_r_changes_mid_leg.fact: A Wear/Failure rate change works at any time and bumps NK_ST_MX_LOG.
rule_r_changes_mid_leg.rule: Normalise each loss with the R that was in force when it happened. With end-of-leg reads only (the ledger's current model), a leg whose MX_LOG step contains a rate-change action cannot be attributed with confidence — flag it 'rate changed mid-leg' for a manual check. No silent guess.
rule_r_changes_mid_leg.cold_start_cylinder_hit: The one-time cold-start cylinder hit (minus 0.05 × R once, SPEC §2.2) is subject to the same normalise-by-R treatment as the continuous losses, not exempt from it.
rule_r_changes_mid_leg.widened_by_the_pro_rata_decision: Under pro rata the flag has to cover more than one posting step. With design 1 (accumulator) it stays as written, because each read is normalised as it happens. With design 2 (snapshot) it must fire whenever R changed at any point since the part was last serviced, not just inside the step that posted.

DECIDED_how_a_normalised_loss_becomes_eu.status: DECIDED — pro rata. Claus, F-BVNK Annunciator board item, 16 Sep 2026 14:47:46 local, relayed word for word by the PM: "Pro rata - bill only the wear that would have happened at REAL". Revision 2 of this kit is collapsed to that single reading; the full-catalogue-price reading is gone.
DECIDED_how_a_normalised_loss_becomes_eu.normalised_points: The points of the part's life the service restores, expressed in REAL-equivalent condition points. Condition runs 0-100, so normalised_points / 100 is the fraction of the part's life actually consumed at REAL rate.
DECIDED_how_a_normalised_loss_becomes_eu.divisor: R for rule_scaled_continuous and rule_scaled_by_r_only, min(R,100) for rule_starter_capped, 1 for rule_never_scaled. R = 0 posts nothing at all (rule_r_zero) and never reaches a divide.
worked_examples: V1 magneto, R=1, serviced from condition 42: observed depletion 100-42 = 58 points, divisor 1, normalised 58.0 → 885.60 × 0.58 = 513.65.
V15 cylinder, R=1000, serviced from condition 35: observed depletion 100-35 = 65 points, divisor 1000, normalised 0.065 → 2767.50 × 0.00065 = 1.80.
V16 brakes, R=100, serviced from condition 70: observed depletion 100-70 = 30 points, divisor 100, normalised 0.3 → 1318.21 × 0.003 = 3.95.
DECIDED_how_a_normalised_loss_becomes_eu.what_this_does_not_touch: Hourly reserves, scheduled 25/50/100 h checks, fuel, aerodrome fees, hangar, insurance and CAO. Every one of those prices off real elapsed hours, litres or the calendar, never off a condition loss, so no divisor reaches them. Also untouched: the laptop ledger FBVNK-LEDGER.html, whose own health model runs on real flown hours with no R in it at all. If that book is ever fed the sim's NK_ST_C_* values, this rule starts applying to it too.
DECIDED_how_a_normalised_loss_becomes_eu.overhaul_is_not_pro_rata: An overhaul (V14) is a whole-unit replacement at its catalogue figure, not a fraction of remaining life. 35,000.00 posts in full whatever the condition was. Same for a battery replacement and a propeller overhaul.

capture_requirement.why: A pro-rata posting needs to know how much life the service restored. A service is detected by the condition reading 100, which is after the fact — by then the pre-service value is gone. Nothing in revision 1 captured it, so pro rata was not computable from what the kit recorded. Named here, per the PM's request, so design note B25 (automatic leg capture) can carry it.

reads_needed_either_way.plus: NK_ST_OIL_QT (quarts, rule_scaled_by_r_only) — same treatment as the ten above.
reads_needed_either_way.plus_R: NK_ST_WEAR, LocalVar 58, already read. The divisor comes from it.
reads_needed_either_way.note: All eleven are existing package variables. No new SimVar, no new reader. What is new is persisting them between reads.

design_1_accumulator_RECOMMENDED.how: On every confirmed (non-reload) read, for each part: drop = previous_condition − current_condition. If drop > 0, add drop / divisor_in_force_now to that part's accumulator. On a service (condition reads 100), bill price_gross × accumulator / 100 and zero the accumulator.
design_1_accumulator_RECOMMENDED.why_this_one: It is exact when R changed during the part's life, because each read is normalised by the R that was actually in force for that read. The snapshot design below is only exact if R never moved since the last service — and a rate change between services is the normal case, not an edge one: R is a slider Claus moves.
design_1_accumulator_RECOMMENDED.count: 22 new persisted LocalVars. Each needs a systems.cfg [LocalVars] entry — package bytes, so a Builder kit and the PM's install, not this session's work.
design_1_accumulator_RECOMMENDED.units: Accumulators hold REAL-equivalent condition points, floating point. Store × 1000 as integers if float drift is a concern; that is a Builder call, the arithmetic is the same.

design_2_snapshot_CHEAPER.how: Persist only the previous read's condition values. On a service, bill price_gross × ((100 − previous_condition) / divisor) / 100.
design_2_snapshot_CHEAPER.new_persisted_variables: The eleven L:NK_LG_PREV_* above, and nothing else. 11 instead of 22.
design_2_snapshot_CHEAPER.the_cost: Exact only when R was constant from the part's last service to this one. If R moved, the whole depletion is divided by whichever R happens to be in force at the moment of service, which is wrong in both directions: service at x1 after wearing the part at x1000 and the posting is 1000× too high. rule_r_changes_mid_leg must then widen from "R changed inside this posting step" to "R changed at any point since this part was last serviced", and flag rather than price.

capture_requirement.for_the_laptop_book: FBVNK-LEDGER.html takes its legs from the aeroplane as records (contract FBVNK_LEG/1). If a record is to carry a service, it carries conditionBefore and conditionAfter as maps keyed by the eleven variable names above, plus the R in force. No persistence problem on that side: the aeroplane holds the snapshot and sends it.

posting_cursor.why_these_two: NK_ST_ENG_HRS is not safe alone — Overhaul sets it to 0 and Reset to delivery sets it to 300 (SPEC §2.1), so it goes backward on purpose. NK_ST_MX_LOG only increments, on every accepted page action, and Reset to delivery does not reset it (SPEC §2.4: '+1 (not reset)'). NK_ST_TACH is never touched by Reset to delivery.
posting_cursor.rule_reload_or_crash: Either number lower than the stored pair (not only TACH with MX_LOG unchanged — a crash can drop both at once) means the sim reloaded a save from before a crash or killed process (assumption, SPEC §1's own hedge: LocalVars save only on a normal exit). Post nothing. Never reverse an invoice already posted. The book stops advancing until BOTH numbers pass the last confirmed point again — no double billing, no silent refund.
posting_cursor.rule_mx_log_higher: MX_LOG higher than stored, on its own, posts the maintenance action(s) it represents.
posting_cursor.rule_tach_higher: TACH higher than stored, on its own, accrues the hourly items (engine/propeller reserves; scheduled-check hour counting).
posting_cursor.rule_independent: Either or both of the above can be true on a given read — this is not an AND condition.

rule_multi_step_jump.fact: A jump of more than 1 in MX_LOG between two reads means more than one action happened at once.

new_install_case.correction_to_first_load_defaults: First-load defaults are the SAME seed values as Reset to delivery, but with MX_LOG 0 (not '+1'). NK_ST_TACH starts at 0 and is then seeded to 1246.58.
new_install_case.detection: A fresh install or a different PC shows the delivery pattern with MX_LOG 0 and TACH below the stored (MX_LOG, TACH) pair — because saved LocalVars do not travel with the package folders.
new_install_case.why_it_matters: Under the posting-cursor rule above, MX_LOG 0 / TACH-below-stored reads as a reload — the book would freeze until both numbers pass the old point, which is wrong for a genuine new install or new machine (Claus plans a move to his CT desktop).
new_install_case.rule: MX_LOG 0 together with the full seed set means 'new install or new machine' — logged, not billed, distinct from an in-sim Reset to delivery action (which advances MX_LOG by 1 instead of showing 0). The cursor is re-baselined only after the pilot confirms it in the ledger. Never automatic.
